svg.title: Linker map: the primer's program, from ELF to flat binary to guest memory
svg.desc: The default layout. The linker places .text (56 bytes, _start first) at 0x4008_0000, .rodata (GREETING, 6 bytes) at 0x4008_0038, .data (BOOTS, 4 bytes) at 0x4008_0040, and .bss (COUNTER plus a 16 KiB stack, 16,400 bytes, NOLOAD) at 0x4008_0050 up to __stack_top at 0x4008_4060. Three PT_LOAD headers: read-execute 56 bytes, read-only 6 bytes, and read-write with FileSize 4 and MemSize 16,416. objcopy -O binary writes 68 bytes: the code, the text hello and a newline, two bytes of padding, and the value 7. The BSS is not in the file; after --raw bare.bin@0x40080000, everything above byte 68 holds whatever RAM held before, so _start must zero it.
svg.text: bare: where the linker puts every byte (default layout)
.bss + stack (16,400 B): old contents of RAM. Zero it yourself!
With JavaScript, the lab lets you move sections, add .far, store a pointer and change the load address.
